initial_observation.encounter_context: Presented with a history of low-backache for the last month; clinical examination identified a single lymph node in the right lower cervical region
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: Patient presented with moderate continuous low-backache for one month and a palpable right lower cervical lymph node present for more than 20 years
presenting_symptoms: Low-backache for the last month, moderate intensity, continuous
Single right lower cervical lymph node swelling (2x2.5 cm), mobile, non-tender, firm
known_prior_history: Right-sided upper neck swelling operated 35 years ago (records unavailable)
Right cervical swelling present for more than 20 years, painless and stable size

evidence_items.source_text: Radiological investigations revealed a lytic lesion in the left acetabulum.

The histopathological examination of the hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) stained sections revealed occasional fragments of dead bone with a few clusters of round to polygonal tumor cells with mild cellular pleomorphism, eccentrically placed round nuclei, coarse chromatin, occasional prominent nucleoli, and a moderate amount of cytoplasm.
evidence_items.temporal_cue: after CT-guided biopsy of acetabular lesion

evidence_items.source_text: Immunohistochemistry revealed the tumor cells to be positive for cytokeratin-7 (CK7) and GATA3 and negative for TTF1 and p63 (Figure 1). Based on the histopathological and immunohistochemical features, a diagnosis of metastatic carcinoma was rendered, with a suggestion of a primary of breast origin.
However, clinical examination, mammography and positron emission tomography (PET) all failed to identify any lesion in the breast or lungs.
evidence_items.temporal_cue: after initial suggestion of breast primary

evidence_items.source_text: The smears were cellular and showed tumor cells predominantly dispersed singly as well as arranged in loose clusters in a background of chondromyxoid stroma. The tumor cells were round to polygonal with mild pleomorphism, eccentrically placed round nuclei, coarse chromatin, occasional prominent nucleoli, and a moderate amount of cytoplasm with some showing cytoplasmic vacuolations. Additionally, occasional loose clusters of relatively smaller cells with scant cytoplasm were also noted (Figure 2).
evidence_items.temporal_cue: at FNAC from right cervical swelling

evidence_items.source_text: The H&E stained section from the cell-block revealed tumor cells arranged in the form of tubules lined by a dual layer of tumor cells. The luminal cells showed a scant to moderate amount of pale to eosinophilic cytoplasm and the basally placed cells showed a moderate amount of clear to vacuolated cytoplasm. A few scattered mitotic figures and occasional lymphoid aggregates were also noted.

On performing IHC, the luminal cells showed strong diffuse membranous positivity for CK7 (epithelial marker) and the abluminal cells showed strong nuclear positivity for p63 (myoepithelial marker). Less than 10% of tumor cells showed nuclear positivity for GATA3 (Figure 3). Based on the cytomorphological features on smears and cell-block and the immunocytochemistry, a final diagnosis of metastatic epithelial-myoepithelial carcinoma was given.

hidden_reference.final_diagnosis_verbatim: a final diagnosis of metastatic epithelial-myoepithelial carcinoma was given.
